new_roles.name: Virtual Intake Coordinator - Adolescent PHP/IOP
new_roles.description:
Virtual Intake Coordinator

Remote in FL | Part-Time | Schedule 3pm-7pm | $17/hour, $19/hour upon completion of training

About the Role
This is a virtual coordinator role supporting AWA's adolescent program with a focus on intakes and administrative support. You keep the program organized and moving by managing intake documentation, coordinating schedules, supporting virtual sessions, and communicating with families throughout the admissions process. Spanish fluency is required for this role.

Backgrounds that translate well: Psychology/Counseling Graduate Studies · Behavioral Health · Case Management · Education · Administrative Support

What You'll Do

  • Process intakes, upload sign-in sheets, prepare welcome kits, and maintain census records
  • Coordinate scheduling for new admissions, including psych and IEP appointments
  • Communicate with parents and families by phone and email in English and Spanish on intake logistics and progress updates
  • Monitor and redirect adolescent clients (ages 13–17) via chat during virtual group sessions and transitions
  • Provide real-time tech support to clients during virtual sessions (Zoom, breakout rooms, chat)
  • Track attendance and maintain accurate program records
  • Complete same-day documentation, including wellness check-ins as needed
  • Escalate safety concerns, disclosures, and behavioral flags to the clinical team immediately

What We're Looking For
Required

  • Bilingual required: English and Spanish
  • Experience in a clinical, educational, administrative, or community mental health setting
  • Comfortable supporting virtual group sessions and managing basic tech troubleshooting (Zoom, breakout rooms)
  • Strong organizational and documentation skills
  • Emotionally regulated, professional, and consistent under pressure
  • Understands the limits of a non-clinical role — escalates appropriately, never makes independent clinical decisions

AWA is an adolescent mental health organization operating PHP and IOP programs in South Florida. We exist to serve teens and families at their most critical moments — and this role is at the center of that work every day.

Learn More: Adolescent Wellness Academy

talent_pool.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,
As a compassionate and detail-oriented mental health professional with over 20 years of experience in behavioral health, I was excited to see the admissions coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a proven track record in admissions coordination, client assessments, case management, and supporting individuals and families through recovery, I am eager to bring my empathy, clinical insight, and organizational strengths to your team.
From 2014 to 2024, I held progressive roles in residential treatment and case management, including serving as Admissions Specialist at Monte Nido, where I managed the full admission process — from initial inquiries and biopsychosocial assessments to insurance coordination and client transitions. I later provided direct care as a Case Manager and Group Facilitator at Recovery is a Beach and Rise Malibu, conducting assessments (including PHQ-9 and GAD-7), developing individualized care plans, facilitating groups, and ensuring seamless coordination with multidisciplinary teams. After welcoming my son in late 2024, I chose to take dedicated time off of work to care for my family. I am now fully refreshed and excited to return to the field with even greater enthusiasm and commitment.
My personal recovery of 22 years continues to fuel my dedication to meeting clients and families with genuine understanding and hope. Whether building rapport with clients and their loved ones, highlighting and explaining the benefits of a particular treatment program, actively listening, collaborating with clinical teams, or maintaining thorough documentation, I bring both professional expertise and heartfelt empathy to every interaction. I am confident my combination of direct admissions experience, case management, group facilitation, strong communication skills, and recovery-informed perspective would enable me to contribute meaningfully from day one.
Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you soon.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Adolescent Services Manager position at AWA. With several years of experience leading youth programs, supervising staff, coordinating daily operations, and creating structured and supportive environments for adolescents, I believe my background in education and youth program management would translate well to this role.

In my current role as an Assistant Director with New York Edge, I help oversee the daily operations of a large after-school program serving more than 500 middle school students. I supervise and coach staff, coordinate schedules and staffing coverage, support program implementation, and step into a site leadership role when the Program Director is unavailable. This experience has strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, maintain structure, address challenges in real time, and ensure that both staff and students have the support they need to be successful.

A significant part of my role involves working directly with adolescents and creating an environment where students feel supported while clear expectations and boundaries are maintained. I have experience responding to behavioral concerns, communicating with families and staff, addressing incidents appropriately, and following established policies and safety procedures. I understand the importance of remaining calm and solutions-focused when unexpected situations arise, while also ensuring consistency and accountability across a team.

I also bring strong organizational and administrative skills. From managing staff schedules and daily program logistics to monitoring attendance, coordinating activities, communicating with multiple stakeholders, and ensuring that program expectations are followed, I am accustomed to keeping complex youth programs running smoothly. I take pride in anticipating potential challenges, identifying solutions, and creating systems that allow both staff and students to have a positive and consistent experience.

My educational background further supports my interest in this position. I hold a Bachelor's degree in Psychology and a Master's degree in School Counseling, which have given me a strong foundation in adolescent development, social-emotional needs, communication, and creating supportive environments for young people. While my professional background has been primarily in education and youth programming rather than clinical mental health services, I am particularly drawn to AWA's focus on providing adolescents and families with a structured, compassionate environment in which they can grow.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my leadership experience, organizational skills, and passion for supporting adolescents to AWA. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to your team and the adolescents and families you serve.

Sincerely,

Leyla Eskinova
